title: SYSK Selects: How Salt Works
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the episode "How Salt Works," introduced by Josh and Chuck as a February episode revisited. The hosts cover salt idioms and etymology (worth one's salt, salary, salad, grain of salt), salt's historical role as currency, preservation and curing, Gandhi's Salt March, the Erie Canal and Civil War salt fights, and the body's need for sodium and electrolytes. They explain hyponatremia and hypernatremia, recommended sodium intake and the CDC's findings on salt and heart risk, and types of salt (table, sea, kosher, rock, Hawaiian and smoked salts). They describe salt mining methods (deep shaft, solution, solar evaporation), the Wieliczka Salt Mine, and religious uses of salt. The episode ends with a listener mail segment responding to a Los Angeles police officer's correction about the Christopher Dorner manhunt shootings, followed by the sign-off.

segments.title: Rerun intro and opening banter
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce this Selects rerun of the salt episode and begin with banter about Josh's love of salt and the show's opening.

segments.title: Salt idioms and etymology
segments.summary: The hosts discuss origins of 'salty,' 'a grain of salt,' 'not worth his salt,' and the link between salary, soldiers' salt rations, and salad.

segments.title: Salt history, Gandhi's Salt March, and preservation
segments.summary: Salt's historical value as currency and a basis for economies, Gandhi's 1930 Salt March against British salt control in India, and salt's role in curing and preserving meat.

segments.title: Salt in history: Erie Canal, colonial production, Civil War
segments.summary: Salt's uses in history, including the Old Salt Route, Massachusetts Bay Colony salt production, the Erie Canal's salt transport, high salt prices in the early 1800s, and Union strategy in the Civil War including the Saltville, Virginia fights.

segments.title: Why the body needs salt
segments.summary: Salt is essential to survival, the body has a dedicated salt taste sense and cravings, and sodium and chlorine form sodium chloride. Electrolytes conduct electrical signals in muscles and the heart.

segments.title: Hyponatremia and hypernatremia
segments.summary: Too little sodium (hyponatremia) and too much sodium (hypernatremia) are described, including water toxicity, kidney function, blood pressure, and historical Chinese salt suicide.

segments.title: Sodium intake recommendations and heart risk
segments.summary: Recommended sodium limits and average American intake are discussed, along with a CDC panel finding that cutting sodium did not clearly reduce heart attack or stroke risk, and advice to check packaged food labels.

segments.title: Types of salt: table salt and iodine
segments.summary: Table salt is discussed, including iodization to prevent goiter and developmental problems, and the Morton Salt girl advertising story and its slogan 'when it rains it pours.'

segments.title: Sea, kosher, rock, and colored salts
segments.summary: Sea salt, pink Himalayan and Hawaiian salts, smoked salt, kosher salt used to draw blood from meat, and rock salt for ice melting and ice cream are described.

segments.title: Salt mining and production methods
segments.summary: Global salt production leaders, deep shaft mining with room-and-pillar systems, the Wieliczka Salt Mine cathedral, solution mining, and solar evaporation are described.

segments.title: Religious significance of salt
segments.summary: Salt's symbolic uses, including the Lot's wife pillar of salt story, a salt pillar near Mount Sodom, and a protective salt shaker in a car glove box, plus a quote from Cassius.

segments.title: Local salt maker plug
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh promote an Atlanta homemade salt maker's products and a website search for the HowStuffWorks article.

segments.title: Listener mail: police chase correction
segments.summary: A Southern California police officer writes that the hosts were wrong about the LAPD shootings during the Christopher Dorner manhunt; he says nobody was killed. Josh says he will double-check and responds that the show respects law enforcement.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck list contact methods and close the episode.
